cases.explain: Погода is the subject of «была» (was), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Железные кровли, плиты ___, голыши мостовой все ярко блестело на майском солнце.
cases.translation: Iron roofs, the paving stones of the sidewalk, the cobbles of the roadway all glittered brightly in the May sunshine.
cases.explain: The genitive here expresses possession/composition ("the paving stones of the sidewalk"), giving тротуара.

cases.sentence: И она вспомнила, как давно-давно, когда ей было еще 17 лет, она ездила с теткой к ___.
cases.translation: And she remembered how long, long ago, when she was still seventeen, she had gone with her aunt to the Trinity monastery.
cases.explain: The preposition к (to/toward) governs the dative case, giving троице.

cases.sentence: Долли одна вышла встретить ___, в эту минуту мешавшую их беседе.
cases.translation: Dolly alone came out to meet the guest, who at that moment was interrupting their conversation.
cases.explain: Гостью is the direct object of the transitive verb встретить (to meet), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Она объясняла эту враждебность неловким ___, в котором теперь чувствовала себя пред ней.
cases.translation: She explained this hostility by the awkward position in which she now felt herself before her.
cases.explain: The instrumental of cause/means after объяснять (to explain) governs положением (position).

cases.sentence: Было три часа и самое оживленное время на ___.
cases.translation: It was three o'clock, the busiest time on the streets.
cases.explain: The preposition на (on) denoting location governs the prepositional case, giving улицах (streets).

reading.question: How was the weather described at the start of the chapter?
reading.explain: The chapter opens: "The weather was clear."

reading.ru: Было три часа и самое оживленное время на улицах.
reading.question: What time was it, and how were the streets described?
options: Three o'clock, the busiest time on the streets
reading.correct: Three o'clock, the busiest time on the streets
reading.explain: The text says it was three o'clock, the busiest time on the streets.

reading.ru: Теперь она упрекала себя за то унижение, до которого она спустилась.
reading.question: What did Anna reproach herself for as she rode in the carriage?
options: The humiliation she had sunk to
reading.correct: The humiliation she had sunk to
reading.explain: The text says she now reproached herself for the humiliation to which she had sunk.

reading.question: What did Anna plan to do regarding Dolly's advice?
options: Follow it, since Dolly loves her
reading.correct: Follow it, since Dolly loves her
reading.explain: Anna tells herself Dolly loves her, and she will follow her advice.

reading.ru: И она вспомнила, как давно-давно, когда ей было еще 17 лет, она ездила с теткой к троице.
reading.question: What memory did Anna recall from when she was seventeen?
options: Traveling with her aunt to the Trinity monastery
reading.correct: Traveling with her aunt to the Trinity monastery
reading.explain: The text says she remembered going with her aunt to the Trinity monastery long ago, when she was seventeen.

reading.question: Who was the man who bowed to Anna on the street?
reading.explain: The text identifies the man who bowed to her as Annushka's husband.

reading.ru: Ужасно то, что нельзя вырвать с корнем прошедшего.
reading.question: What did Anna think was terrible about the past?
options: That it cannot be torn out by the root
reading.correct: That it cannot be torn out by the root
reading.explain: Anna reflects that it is terrible that one cannot tear out the past by its root.

reading.ru: Три мальчика бегут, играя в лошадки.
reading.question: What did Anna notice on the boulevard?
reading.explain: The text mentions the boulevard and three boys running, playing at horses.

reading.ru: Придумывая те слова, в которых она все скажет Долли, и умышленно растравляя свое сердце, Анна вошла на лестницу.
reading.question: What was Anna doing as she climbed the stairs to Dolly's apartment?
options: Rehearsing what she would tell Dolly, deliberately tormenting her own heart
reading.correct: Rehearsing what she would tell Dolly, deliberately tormenting her own heart
reading.explain: The text says that, composing the words she would say to Dolly and deliberately inflaming her heart, Anna climbed the stairs.

reading.ru: Та самая Китти, в которую был влюблен Вронский», — подумала Анна.
reading.question: Who did Anna think of upon hearing the name "Kitty"?
options: The very Kitty that Vronsky had once been in love with
reading.correct: The very Kitty that Vronsky had once been in love with
reading.explain: Anna thinks: "the very Kitty with whom Vronsky had been in love."

reading.ru: Долли одна вышла встретить гостью, в эту минуту мешавшую их беседе.
reading.question: Who came out alone to meet Anna when she arrived?
reading.explain: The text says Dolly came out alone to meet her guest.

reading.ru: «Я не надеюсь, да и не желаю», — сказала Анна.
reading.question: What did Anna say about hoping for a resolution to the divorce?
options: That she neither hoped for nor wished for it
That she didn't care either way
That she wanted to speak to Karenin herself
reading.correct: That she neither hoped for nor wished for it
reading.explain: Anna says, "I don't hope, and I don't wish it."

reading.question: What did Dolly bring in?
reading.explain: The text says Dolly came in with the letter.

reading.ru: «Я очень рада», — сказала она дрожащим голосом.
reading.question: How did Kitty greet Anna?
options: Saying "I am very glad" in a trembling voice
reading.correct: Saying "I am very glad" in a trembling voice
reading.explain: The text says Kitty said, "I am very glad," in a trembling voice.

reading.ru: Они поговорили про болезнь, про ребенка, про Стиву, но, очевидно, ничто не интересовало Анну.
reading.question: What topics did Anna, Dolly, and Kitty discuss, though nothing interested Anna?
reading.explain: The text says they talked about the illness, the baby, and Stiva, but nothing evidently interested Anna.

reading.ru: «Когда я ее провожала в передней, мне показалось, что она хочет плакать».
reading.question: What did Dolly notice as she saw Anna out?
options: That Anna seemed as if she wanted to cry
reading.correct: That Anna seemed as if she wanted to cry
reading.explain: The chapter ends with Dolly saying that as she saw Anna out, it seemed to her that Anna wanted to cry.

highlight.question: Which sentence lists the various objects that were shining brightly in the sunlight?
sentences: Погода была ясная.
Все утро шел частый, мелкий дождик, и теперь недавно прояснило.
Железные кровли, плиты тротуаров, голыши мостовой, колеса и кожи, медь и жесть экипажей – все ярко блестело на майском солнце.
Было три часа и самое оживленное время на улицах.
highlight.explain: Sentence 2 catalogs roofs, pavement tiles, wheels, leather, brass, and other surfaces gleaming in the May sun.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Anna attempting to resolve or confront the situation with Vronsky?
sentences: Поверила ли бы я тогда, что я могу дойти до такого унижения?
Как он будет горд и доволен, получив мою записку!
Но я докажу ему…
Как дурно пахнет эта краска.
Зачем они все красят и строят?
highlight.explain: Sentence 2 expresses Anna's determination with But I will prove to him, indicating her resolve to take action.

highlight.question: Which sentence expresses Anna's belief about how Vronsky currently views her?
sentences: «Кити!  та самая Кити, в которую был влюблен Вронский, – подумала Анна, – та самая, про которую он вспоминал с любовью.
Он жалеет, что не женился на ней.
А обо мне он вспоминает с ненавистью и жалеет, что сошелся со мной».
highlight.explain: Sentence 2 states that Vronsky remembers her with hatred and regrets their involvement.

highlight.question: Which sentence emphasizes what Anna gave up for Vronsky from the very beginning?
sentences: Я знаю, что с той первой минуты я пожертвовала ему всем!
И вот награда!
О, как я ненавижу его!
И зачем я приехала сюда?
Мне еще хуже, еще тяжелее, – Она слышала из другой комнаты голоса переговаривавшихся сестер.
highlight.explain: Sentence 0 stresses that from the first moment Anna sacrificed everything for him.

highlight.question: Which sentence reveals that Dolly had never witnessed Anna in her current emotional state?
sentences: – Да отчего же?
Я, напротив, надеюсь, – сказала Долли, с любопытством глядя на Анну.
Она никогда не видела ее в таком странном раздраженном состоянии.
– Ты когда едешь?
– спросила она.
highlight.explain: Sentence 2 notes that Dolly had never seen Anna so strangely irritated before.

highlight.question: Which sentence reveals Dolly's difficulty in being dishonest about someone's whereabouts?
sentences: – Ах, какие пустяки!
Она кормит, и у нее не ладится дело, я ей советовала…
Она очень рада.
Она сейчас придет, – неловко, не умея говорить неправду, говорила Долли.
– Да вот и она.
highlight.explain: Sentence 3 explicitly notes that Dolly spoke awkwardly, unable to lie well.
